The suspect, identified by her DMV photo as Angelica, was taken to Hancock County Justice Center. According to court documents, she was charged with two counts of failure to comply with an order and theft. Despite her threats of having the best lawyers, she was assigned a public defender and her bond was set to $25,000. Her trial date is set for August 25, 2025, which will be her first case in Hancock County. However, a search of her case history in neighboring Toledo County revealed 17 different motor vehicle violations, including one for having an unbuckled child in her car. Now, what will make a simple-dick sporting goods retail theft call spiral into a multi-police agency pursuit? The answer is pretty simple, failure to take accountability and running. And some might think that the more police that are involved might get this resolved quicker, but that's not always the case. And the biggest issue in this Ohio incident wasn't the escaping criminal. It was the inability of the officers to communicate to each other. And trust me, it wasn't because of bad police work. Because imagine just for argument's sake there's four different departments, with their own radio systems, their own supervisors, and their own pursuit policies, and they're all chasing one suspect. It could be confusing and chaotic. Commands can be missed, and units may double up or be left behind. But in Minnesota, all law enforcement channels are digital. which allows them to have statewide channels for pursuits called LTACS, along every officer in the state to hear a chase if needed. Additionally, there are other statewide tactical channels that allow police, fire, and medics to be all in the same channel, talking about the same incident. The beauty of Minnesota system is whenever an officer goes into pursuit, every other officer in the state immediately hears it. But I'll leave you with this. If Minnesota can build a system that unites cops, medics, and firefighters on the same channel, would stop in these other states. Is it politics, funding, or just a lack of will from the people in charge? So of course, let us know what you guys think. Should all states adopt the unified radio system, Or is it just part of the job?
